prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CCCS(=O)(=O)Nc1ccc(F)c(C(=O)c2c[nH]c3ncc(-c4ccc(Cl)cc4)cc23)c1F
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL5145

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of BRAF V600E mutant (unknown origin) after 1 to 1.5 hrs by FRET-based Z'-Lyte assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of recombinant human N-terminal GST-tagged BRAF catalytic domain (416 to 766 residues) V600E mutant expressed in baculovirus expression system using human His6-tagged MEK1 K97R mutant as substrate pretreated for 20 mins followed by [33P]-ATP addition measured after 2 hrs by filter binding method
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "INSUFFICIENT_INFO", "confidence": 0.5, "error_class": "assay_method", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 against BRAF V600E with high confidence and the same organism, but differ in detection method (FRET-based Z'-Lyte vs. radiometric filter binding), substrate (generic kinase substrate vs. MEK1 K97R), construct details (full-length vs. catalytic domain 416-766), and incubation times, making it uncertain whether results will agree within 0.3 log units or diverge beyond 1.0 log units."}
